def fruit_distribution(s,n):
    
    lis = list()
    for i in s.split(' '):
        if i.isdigit():
            lis.append(int(i))
    return n - sum(lis)

# Unit test for function fruit_distribution
def test_fruit_distribution():
    # Basic case: digits and words mixed
    assert fruit_distribution("5 apples and 6 oranges", 19) == 8
    # Single number in string
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 1 oranges", 3) == 2
    # Multiple multi-digit numbers
    assert fruit_distribution("10 apples and 20 oranges", 100) == 70
    # No digits at all - all fruits are mangoes
    assert fruit_distribution("apples and oranges", 15) == 15
    # Zero total fruits
    assert fruit_distribution("0 apples and 0 oranges", 0) == 0
    # Result can be zero when digits sum to n
    assert fruit_distribution("3 apples and 7 oranges", 10) == 0
    # Large numbers
    assert fruit_distribution("1000 apples and 2000 oranges", 5000) == 2000
    # Repeated numbers in string
    assert fruit_distribution("2 apples and 2 oranges and 2 bananas", 10) == 4
    # Number followed immediately by punctuation (not digit-attached)
    assert fruit_distribution("1 apple, 2 oranges", 5) == 2
    # All fruits are accounted for except mangoes, large n
    assert fruit_distribution("1 apples and 1 oranges", 1000) == 998

    print("All tests passed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_fruit_distribution()
